name: Honey BBQ Chicken Mac and Cheese

intro_html: There is a particular kind of comfort in a bowl of mac and cheese, and usually a particular kind of guilt riding along with it. This one keeps the comfort and leaves the guilt at the door. We blend fat free cottage cheese, light cream cheese, and reduced fat cheddar into a sauce that eats like the real thing, then crown every bowl with honey BBQ chicken that caramelizes right in the pan. It lands at {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein a serving, which is the kind of math that lets you go back for a second look at the container with a clear conscience. Fourteen servings, one afternoon, dinner handled all week.

cost_closing_html: Here is where it gets good. All fourteen servings, chicken and cheese and pasta included, come out to ${{cost_ps}} a serving. That is restaurant comfort food for the price of a vending machine snack, and it is built on cottage cheese and cream cheese instead of a pan of butter and flour. Cook it once, eat it all week, and let the numbers do the arguing.
shop_smart: The cheese sauce is doing the heavy lifting here, so shop the dairy first. You need 2 1/3 cups of fat free cottage cheese, 1 1/2 pounds of light cream cheese, and 4 3/4 cups of shredded reduced fat cheddar. Buy the cheddar however your store sells it plainest, block or bag, because it all goes in the blender anyway. Round it out with 2 1/4 cups of milk. The chicken is 3 pounds of boneless skinless breast, diced, and the pasta is 2 1/3 pounds dry. The honey BBQ side is small: 7 tablespoons of honey and 3/4 cup plus 2 tablespoons of BBQ sauce. Here is the quiet efficiency of this recipe. The garlic powder, paprika, black pepper, and salt each get bought one time and then pull double duty, seasoning the chicken and going into the sauce, so nothing in the spice aisle sits on the shelf unused.
make_it: Start with the chicken, because it wants a head start. Season your 3 pounds of diced chicken breast with garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, ground ginger, salt, and black pepper.

You have two roads here. Air fryer people, preheat to 350F, spray the chicken lightly with cooking spray, and cook 10 to 12 minutes, shaking the basket halfway, until it is golden and cooked through. Stovetop people, heat a non-stick pan over medium, hit it with cooking spray, and cook the chicken 6 to 8 minutes until browned and done.
Either way, once it is cooked, toss it in a bowl with the honey and BBQ sauce until every piece is coated, then give it another 1 to 2 minutes over the heat to let that glaze caramelize.

Now the pasta. Bring a big pot of salted water to a boil and cook your pasta to the package directions. Before you drain, dip out about a quarter cup of the pasta water and set it aside, because that starchy water is your secret for a loose, creamy sauce. Drain and hold.

The sauce is a blender job, which is the whole trick to keeping this light. Combine the cottage cheese, cream cheese, shredded cheddar, milk, garlic powder, parsley, black pepper, paprika, salt, and mustard, and blend until it is smooth and creamy.
Pour it into a saucepan over medium-low heat and stir, cooking 3 to 5 minutes until it thickens up. If it gets too thick on you, splash in some of that reserved pasta water.
Stir the drained pasta into the sauce until every noodle is coated, adding more pasta water until it looks right to you.

Then walk away for 10 minutes. Letting it rest is what pulls the flavors together and sets the sauce. Portion it into bowls, top each one with the honey BBQ chicken, and finish with a sprinkle of parsley.
portion_html: Fourteen servings out of one batch, so a kitchen scale earns its keep here. Weigh your empty container, then weigh the full pot of mac and cheese with the chicken kept separate, subtract the container, and divide that pasta total by 14. Scoop the same weight into every container so nobody gets shorted on the cheesy part. Then split the honey BBQ chicken evenly across all fourteen and lay it on top. Eyeballing it means the first few bowls run rich and the last few run sad, and the scale fixes that in about a minute.

head.description: High protein honey BBQ chicken mac and cheese meal prep. A blended cottage and cream cheese sauce over pasta, topped with caramelized honey BBQ chicken. Fourteen servings.

steps: Season the 3 pounds of diced chicken breast with garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, ground ginger, salt, and black pepper.
Cook the chicken: air fry at 350F for 10 to 12 minutes shaking halfway, or pan fry over medium heat with cooking spray for 6 to 8 minutes, until golden and cooked through.
Toss the cooked chicken with the honey and BBQ sauce, then cook 1 to 2 minutes more to caramelize the glaze.
Boil the pasta in salted water. Reserve about a quarter cup of pasta water, then drain and set aside.
Blend the cottage cheese, cream cheese, shredded cheddar, milk, garlic powder, parsley, black pepper, paprika, salt, and mustard until smooth and creamy.
Heat the cheese sauce in a saucepan over medium-low for 3 to 5 minutes, loosening with reserved pasta water if it thickens too much.
Stir the drained pasta into the sauce until evenly coated, adding pasta water to reach the consistency you want.
Let it rest 10 minutes to thicken, then portion into bowls and top each with the honey BBQ chicken and a sprinkle of parsley.
